examples.english: She took full ownership of the project after the previous lead left.
examples.persian: او پس از رفتن مسئول قبلی، مالکیت کامل پروژه را بر عهده گرفت.

examples.english: Taking ownership of a mistake is more important than assigning blame.
examples.persian: پذیرفتن مسئولیت یک اشتباه مهم‌تر از مقصر دانستن دیگران است.

examples.english: Managers want to see ownership, not just task completion, from senior engineers.
examples.persian: مدیران از مهندسان ارشد انتظار مسئولیت‌پذیری دارند، نه فقط تکمیل وظایف.

miniContext: In many companies, **ownership** means more than doing assigned tasks — it means caring about whether the product actually works and taking responsibility when it doesn't. An engineer with ownership will fix a bug discovered late on a Friday even if nobody asked them to. Managers often look for ownership during performance reviews because it signals that someone can be trusted with bigger responsibilities. Teams with strong ownership tend to need less supervision.

examples.english: Accountability means answering for the outcome of your decisions, not just your effort.
examples.persian: پاسخ‌گویی به معنای پاسخگو بودن در برابر نتیجه تصمیم‌هایتان است، نه فقط تلاشی که کرده‌اید.

examples.english: Without clear accountability, no one on the team felt responsible for the failed deployment.
examples.persian: بدون پاسخ‌گویی روشن، هیچ‌کس در تیم خودش را مسئول استقرار ناموفق نمی‌دانست.

examples.english: The new manager introduced weekly reviews to strengthen accountability across the team.
examples.persian: مدیر جدید جلسات بررسی هفتگی را برای تقویت پاسخ‌گویی در تیم معرفی کرد.

miniContext: **Accountability** is closely related to ownership, but it focuses specifically on answering for results. A team can have accountability structures, such as clear owners for each service, so that when something breaks, there is no confusion about who should respond. Accountability also works in the other direction: managers are accountable to their teams for setting realistic expectations. Without accountability, failures tend to repeat because no one examines what went wrong.

examples.english: Good collaboration between design and engineering reduced the number of last-minute changes.
examples.persian: همکاری خوب بین تیم طراحی و مهندسی تعداد تغییرات لحظه آخری را کاهش داد.

examples.english: The hackathon encouraged collaboration among employees who rarely worked together.
examples.persian: هکاتون همکاری میان کارمندانی را که به‌ندرت با هم کار می‌کردند تشویق کرد.

examples.english: She praised the team's collaboration during the stressful product launch.
examples.persian: او از همکاری تیم در طول عرضه پراسترس محصول تقدیر کرد.

miniContext: Modern software projects rarely succeed through individual effort alone; they depend on **collaboration** between designers, engineers, and product managers. Good collaboration means sharing context early, rather than working in isolation and discovering conflicts at the last minute. Tools like shared documents and pair programming are often used to support collaboration across time zones. Teams that collaborate well usually catch problems sooner.

examples.english: A cross-functional team was formed to launch the new feature on time.
examples.persian: یک تیم بین‌تیمی برای عرضه به‌موقع ویژگی جدید تشکیل شد.

examples.english: She has experience leading cross-functional projects that involve marketing, design, and engineering.
examples.persian: او تجربه رهبری پروژه‌های بین‌تیمی شامل بازاریابی، طراحی و مهندسی را دارد.

examples.english: Cross-functional communication can be difficult when teams use different tools and terminology.
examples.persian: ارتباط بین‌تیمی زمانی که تیم‌ها از ابزارها و اصطلاحات متفاوت استفاده می‌کنند می‌تواند دشوار باشد.

miniContext: A **cross-functional** team brings together people from different departments, such as engineering, design, and marketing, to work toward a single goal. Cross-functional work can be harder to coordinate because each group may use different terminology and priorities. However, it often produces better results than departments working separately, since decisions are made with a fuller picture. Companies increasingly favor cross-functional structures for product launches.

examples.english: Clear communication between the client and the team prevented several misunderstandings.
examples.persian: ارتباط روشن میان مشتری و تیم چندین سوءتفاهم را از بین برد.

examples.english: Poor communication during the handover left the new hire confused about her responsibilities.
examples.persian: ارتباط ضعیف در زمان تحویل کار، کارمند جدید را درباره وظایفش گیج کرد.

examples.english: The manager emphasized communication as the most important skill for remote teams.
examples.persian: مدیر بر ارتباطات به‌عنوان مهم‌ترین مهارت برای تیم‌های دورکار تأکید کرد.

miniContext: **Communication** failures are one of the most common causes of project delays, even when everyone involved is technically skilled. Clear communication means sharing not just decisions, but also the reasoning behind them, so other people can act correctly without constant follow-up questions. In remote teams, communication often has to be more deliberate, since quick hallway conversations aren't possible. Writing things down is one of the simplest ways to improve communication.

examples.english: He explained the technical concept in simple terms so the stakeholders could follow along.
examples.persian: او مفهوم فنی را به زبان ساده توضیح داد تا ذی‌نفعان بتوانند آن را دنبال کنند.

examples.english: Understanding this technical concept took the new intern almost a full week.
examples.persian: درک این مفهوم فنی تقریباً یک هفته کامل از کارآموز جدید وقت گرفت.

examples.english: The interviewer asked her to describe a difficult technical concept to a non-technical audience.
examples.persian: مصاحبه‌کننده از او خواست یک مفهوم فنی دشوار را برای مخاطبان غیرفنی توضیح دهد.

miniContext: Explaining a **technical concept** clearly to a non-technical audience is a skill that many engineers have to develop over time. A good explanation usually relies on analogies and avoids unnecessary jargon, without oversimplifying the idea to the point of being inaccurate. Interviewers sometimes test this skill directly, asking candidates to describe a technical concept to someone outside the field. Being able to translate a technical concept into plain language is valuable in meetings with clients and stakeholders.

examples.english: The final decision rested with the product manager, not the engineering team.
examples.persian: تصمیم نهایی با مدیر محصول بود، نه با تیم مهندسی.

examples.english: She regretted her decision to accept the offer without negotiating the salary.
examples.persian: او از تصمیمش برای پذیرفتن پیشنهاد بدون مذاکره درباره حقوق پشیمان شد.

examples.english: Every decision in the retrospective was documented so the team could review it later.
examples.persian: هر تصمیم در جلسه بازنگری ثبت شد تا تیم بتواند بعداً آن را بررسی کند.

miniContext: Every project involves dozens of small and large decisions, from which library to use to how to handle an edge case. A good **decision** doesn't require perfect information; it requires weighing the available evidence and accepting some risk. Teams that document their decisions, along with the reasoning behind them, make it easier to revisit those choices later. Avoiding a decision for too long can be just as costly as making the wrong one.

examples.english: The client changed a key requirement halfway through the sprint.
examples.persian: مشتری یک نیازمندی کلیدی را در میانه اسپرینت تغییر داد.

examples.english: Each requirement must be approved before the development team starts working on it.
examples.persian: هر نیازمندی باید پیش از شروع کار تیم توسعه تأیید شود.

examples.english: The missing requirement caused confusion during the final testing phase.
examples.persian: نیازمندی ازقلم‌افتاده در مرحله نهایی آزمایش باعث سردرگمی شد.

miniContext: A **requirement** describes what a system or feature must do, and getting requirements wrong early in a project can be expensive to fix later. Requirements sometimes change as stakeholders learn more about what they actually need, which is why flexible processes exist to handle updates. Engineers often ask clarifying questions to make sure a requirement is specific enough to build correctly. Ambiguous requirements are one of the most common sources of rework.

examples.english: Good stakeholder management kept the marketing and legal teams aligned throughout the project.
examples.persian: مدیریت خوب ذی‌نفعان تیم‌های بازاریابی و حقوقی را در طول پروژه هم‌راستا نگه داشت.

examples.english: Weak stakeholder management led to conflicting priorities between departments.
examples.persian: مدیریت ضعیف ذی‌نفعان باعث تضاد اولویت‌ها میان بخش‌ها شد.

examples.english: The course teaches stakeholder management skills such as negotiation and expectation setting.
examples.persian: این دوره مهارت‌های مدیریت ذی‌نفعان مانند مذاکره و تعیین انتظارات را آموزش می‌دهد.

miniContext: **Stakeholder management** involves keeping everyone with an interest in a project, such as clients, executives, and other teams, informed and aligned. It often requires balancing conflicting priorities, since different stakeholders may want different things from the same project. Effective stakeholder management includes setting realistic expectations early, rather than promising more than a team can deliver. Project managers spend a significant part of their time on stakeholder management rather than on the technical work itself.

examples.english: Problem solving is tested heavily during the technical interview.
examples.persian: حل مسئله در طول مصاحبه فنی به‌شدت سنجیده می‌شود.

examples.english: Her problem solving under pressure impressed the entire panel.
examples.persian: توانایی او در حل مسئله تحت فشار کل هیئت داوران را تحت تأثیر قرار داد.

examples.english: The workshop focused on problem solving techniques for debugging production issues.
examples.persian: این کارگاه بر تکنیک‌های حل مسئله برای رفع اشکالات محیط عملیاتی تمرکز داشت.

miniContext: **Problem solving** is one of the most tested skills in technical interviews, often through coding exercises or system design questions. It involves breaking a large, unclear issue into smaller parts that can be investigated and solved one at a time. Strong problem solving also means knowing when to ask for help instead of struggling alone for too long. Experienced engineers tend to rely on structured problem solving rather than guessing randomly.

examples.english: Decision-making became slower once every change required approval from three departments.
examples.persian: تصمیم‌گیری پس از آن‌که هر تغییر به تأیید سه بخش نیاز داشت، کندتر شد.

examples.english: The company values fast decision-making over long discussions in meetings.
examples.persian: این شرکت تصمیم‌گیری سریع را بر بحث‌های طولانی در جلسات ترجیح می‌دهد.

examples.english: Her decision-making improved once she had access to accurate data.
examples.persian: تصمیم‌گیری او پس از دسترسی به داده‌های دقیق بهبود یافت.

miniContext: **Decision-making** in organizations can be slow when too many people need to approve every choice. Some companies try to speed up decision-making by giving individual teams more autonomy over their own areas. Good decision-making depends on having access to relevant data, not just intuition or seniority. Poor decision-making often traces back to unclear ownership over who is actually responsible for the outcome.

examples.english: He prefers a decision-oriented meeting where every discussion ends with a clear outcome.
examples.persian: او جلسه‌ای متمرکز بر تصمیم را ترجیح می‌دهد که هر بحث با نتیجه روشنی پایان یابد.

examples.english: The new manager runs a more decision-oriented standup than the previous one.
examples.persian: مدیر جدید جلسه ایستاده‌ای متمرکزتر بر تصمیم نسبت به مدیر قبلی برگزار می‌کند.

examples.english: Being decision-oriented helped her move the project forward instead of getting stuck in analysis.
examples.persian: متمرکز بودن بر تصمیم به او کمک کرد پروژه را جلو ببرد به‌جای گیر افتادن در تحلیل بیش‌ازحد.

miniContext: A **decision-oriented** meeting is designed to end with a clear outcome, rather than simply exchanging updates. Teams that run decision-oriented discussions usually prepare an agenda in advance and assign someone to make the final call if there is disagreement. Being decision-oriented doesn't mean rushing; it means making sure that time spent discussing something actually leads somewhere. Many engineers find decision-oriented meetings far less draining than open-ended ones.

examples.english: The implementation took longer than expected because of an outdated library.
examples.persian: پیاده‌سازی به دلیل یک کتابخانه قدیمی بیشتر از حد انتظار طول کشید.

examples.english: Before implementation begins, the team reviews the design document together.
examples.persian: پیش از شروع پیاده‌سازی، تیم سند طراحی را با هم بررسی می‌کند.

examples.english: A poor implementation of the caching logic caused the outage last week.
examples.persian: پیاده‌سازی ضعیف منطق کش باعث قطعی هفته گذشته شد.

miniContext: **Implementation** is the stage where a design or plan is actually turned into working code. Even a well-thought-out design can run into unexpected problems once implementation begins, such as a library behaving differently than documented. Reviewing an implementation carefully, rather than just checking that it compiles, helps catch subtle bugs before release. Teams often underestimate how long implementation will take compared to planning.

examples.english: The team committed to a delivery date that proved unrealistic.
examples.persian: تیم به تاریخ تحویلی متعهد شد که غیرواقعی از آب درآمد.

examples.english: Consistent delivery builds more trust with stakeholders than occasional heroics.
examples.persian: تحویل منظم اعتماد بیشتری نسبت به قهرمانی‌های گاه‌به‌گاه در ذی‌نفعان ایجاد می‌کند.

examples.english: The delay in delivery forced the marketing team to postpone the launch.
examples.persian: تأخیر در تحویل، تیم بازاریابی را مجبور به عقب انداختن عرضه محصول کرد.

miniContext: **Delivery** refers to getting finished work into the hands of users, whether that means shipping a feature or releasing a report. Reliable delivery builds trust with stakeholders, since they can plan around dates that are actually met. Some teams prioritize frequent, smaller deliveries over large, infrequent ones, because smaller releases are easier to test and roll back. A missed delivery date can affect other teams who were depending on that work being finished.

examples.english: The team missed the deadline because the requirements changed too late.
examples.persian: تیم به دلیل تغییر دیرهنگام نیازمندی‌ها از مهلت تعیین‌شده عقب ماند.

examples.english: She asked for an extended deadline to properly test the new feature.
examples.persian: او برای آزمایش درست ویژگی جدید، مهلت بیشتری خواست.

examples.english: A tight deadline pushed the developers to skip writing proper tests.
examples.persian: مهلت فشرده باعث شد توسعه‌دهندگان از نوشتن آزمون‌های درست صرف‌نظر کنند.

miniContext: A **deadline** sets a fixed point by which work must be completed, and how realistic that deadline is often determines the quality of the final result. Tight deadlines can push teams to cut corners, skipping tests or documentation to finish on time. Experienced managers try to negotiate deadlines based on actual scope, rather than accepting arbitrary dates set by someone outside the team. Missing a deadline is sometimes less damaging than hiding the fact that it will be missed.

examples.english: Fixing the security bug became the team's top priority.
examples.persian: رفع باگ امنیتی به اولویت اصلی تیم تبدیل شد.

examples.english: The manager had to explain why the client's request was not a priority this sprint.
examples.persian: مدیر باید توضیح می‌داد چرا درخواست مشتری در این اسپرینت اولویت نداشت.

examples.english: When everything is labeled urgent, nothing is actually a priority.
examples.persian: وقتی همه‌چیز فوری برچسب‌گذاری شود، در واقع هیچ‌چیز اولویت ندارد.

miniContext: Deciding what is a **priority** means deciding what gets attention first when time and resources are limited. When every task is labeled as a priority, teams lose the ability to actually focus on what matters most. Priorities often need to be revisited as new information arrives, such as a critical bug appearing during a planned feature release. Clear priorities make it easier for a team to say no to less important requests.

examples.english: Migrating the legacy database was the biggest challenge of the project.
examples.persian: مهاجرت پایگاه‌داده قدیمی بزرگ‌ترین چالش پروژه بود.

examples.english: She described the staffing shortage as a challenge rather than a crisis.
examples.persian: او کمبود نیرو را به‌عنوان یک چالش توصیف کرد نه یک بحران.

examples.english: Every new hire faces the challenge of learning the company's internal tools.
examples.persian: هر کارمند تازه‌استخدام با چالش یادگیری ابزارهای داخلی شرکت روبرو می‌شود.

miniContext: Every project brings its own **challenge**, whether it's a technical limitation, a tight deadline, or disagreement between stakeholders. Framing a difficult situation as a challenge rather than a disaster can help a team stay focused on solutions. Some challenges can be solved with more resources, while others require a completely different approach. Interviewers often ask candidates to describe a challenge they faced and how they handled it.

examples.english: The on-call engineer was paged as soon as the incident was detected.
examples.persian: مهندس آن‌کال به محض شناسایی رخداد عملیاتی فراخوانده شد.

examples.english: The postmortem document explained the root cause of the incident in detail.
examples.persian: سند پس از رخداد، علت اصلی رخداد عملیاتی را به‌تفصیل توضیح داد.

examples.english: This was the third incident this month caused by the same misconfigured server.
examples.persian: این سومین رخداد عملیاتی این ماه بود که به دلیل همان سرور با پیکربندی نادرست رخ داد.

miniContext: An **incident** is an unplanned event, such as an outage or data issue, that disrupts normal operations. When an incident occurs, the priority is usually to restore service first and investigate the root cause afterward. Teams often write a postmortem after a serious incident to understand what went wrong and prevent it from happening again. Repeated incidents from the same cause usually point to a problem that was never properly fixed.

examples.english: The new caching layer led to a noticeable improvement in page load time.
examples.persian: لایه کش جدید باعث بهبود قابل‌توجهی در زمان بارگذاری صفحه شد.

examples.english: Her manager pointed out areas for improvement during the performance review.
examples.persian: مدیرش در بررسی عملکرد به زمینه‌های قابل بهبود اشاره کرد.

examples.english: Continuous improvement is one of the team's core engineering values.
examples.persian: بهبود پیوسته یکی از ارزش‌های اصلی مهندسی تیم است.

miniContext: Small, steady **improvement** often matters more over time than occasional large changes. A performance review might highlight areas for improvement, such as communication or time management, alongside existing strengths. Teams that track metrics can measure whether a change actually led to improvement or just felt like it did. Continuous improvement requires being willing to admit that the current approach isn't perfect.

examples.english: The growth team ran an experiment to test two different signup flows.
examples.persian: تیم رشد یک آزمایش برای سنجش دو روند متفاوت ثبت‌نام اجرا کرد.

examples.english: The experiment showed no significant difference between the two designs.
examples.persian: آزمایش هیچ تفاوت معناداری بین دو طراحی نشان نداد.

examples.english: Before changing the pricing page permanently, they wanted to run a small experiment.
examples.persian: پیش از تغییر دائمی صفحه قیمت‌گذاری، آن‌ها می‌خواستند یک آزمایش کوچک اجرا کنند.

miniContext: Running an **experiment**, such as an A/B test, allows a team to check whether an idea actually works before rolling it out to everyone. A good experiment isolates one variable at a time, so the results clearly show what caused the change. Not every experiment succeeds, and a failed experiment can still provide useful information about what doesn't work. Teams that experiment regularly tend to make decisions based on evidence rather than opinion.

examples.english: Mentoring junior developers takes up a significant part of her week.
examples.persian: منتورینگ توسعه‌دهندگان جونیور بخش قابل‌توجهی از هفته او را می‌گیرد.

examples.english: The company launched a formal mentoring program for new graduates.
examples.persian: شرکت یک برنامه رسمی منتورینگ برای فارغ‌التحصیلان جدید راه‌اندازی کرد.

examples.english: He credits his growth as an engineer to the mentoring he received early in his career.
examples.persian: او پیشرفتش به‌عنوان یک مهندس را به منتورینگی که در آغاز مسیر شغلی‌اش دریافت کرد، نسبت می‌دهد.

miniContext: **Mentoring** involves a more experienced person helping someone else grow, often through regular conversations rather than formal lessons. Good mentoring focuses on asking questions that help the other person think through a problem, instead of simply giving the answer. Companies that invest in mentoring programs often see new hires become productive more quickly. Mentoring relationships work best when both people see clear value in the time they spend together.

examples.english: Good coaching helped the junior engineer gain confidence in code reviews.
examples.persian: مربی‌گری خوب به مهندس جونیور کمک کرد در بازبینی کد اعتمادبه‌نفس پیدا کند.

examples.english: The team lead offers coaching sessions instead of simply assigning tasks.
examples.persian: سرپرست تیم به‌جای صرفاً واگذار کردن وظایف، جلسات مربی‌گری ارائه می‌دهد.

examples.english: Coaching focuses on asking the right questions rather than giving direct answers.
examples.persian: مربی‌گری بر پرسیدن سؤالات درست تمرکز دارد نه ارائه پاسخ‌های مستقیم.

miniContext: **Coaching** at work is similar to mentoring but often focuses more narrowly on improving a specific skill or habit. A manager who does coaching might sit with an engineer during a difficult code review to help them think through the feedback, rather than fixing it for them. Coaching requires patience, since the goal is long-term growth rather than a quick fix. Some companies train their managers specifically in coaching techniques.

examples.english: She left her previous job because it offered no room for growth.
examples.persian: او شغل قبلی‌اش را ترک کرد چون فرصتی برای رشد نداشت.

examples.english: Rapid growth forced the company to hire three new managers in one quarter.
examples.persian: رشد سریع شرکت را مجبور کرد در یک فصل سه مدیر جدید استخدام کند.

examples.english: He asked his manager directly about his growth opportunities within the team.
examples.persian: او مستقیماً از مدیرش درباره فرصت‌های رشد خود در تیم پرسید.

miniContext: Career **growth** usually matters as much to employees as salary, especially for people early in their careers. A lack of growth opportunities is one of the most common reasons people leave a job, even when they are otherwise satisfied. Growth can come from new responsibilities, a different project, or simply learning a new skill. Managers who ignore growth conversations risk losing their strongest performers.

examples.english: Her curiosity about how the system worked led her to read the entire codebase.
examples.persian: کنجکاوی او درباره نحوه کار سیستم باعث شد کل کدبیس را مطالعه کند.

examples.english: Interviewers often look for curiosity rather than just memorized answers.
examples.persian: مصاحبه‌کنندگان معمولاً به‌جای پاسخ‌های حفظ‌شده، به دنبال کنجکاوی هستند.

examples.english: His curiosity pushed him to ask why the old system had been designed that way.
examples.persian: کنجکاوی او باعث شد بپرسد چرا سیستم قدیمی به آن شکل طراحی شده بود.

miniContext: **Curiosity** drives people to ask why something works the way it does, instead of just accepting it. Hiring managers often value curiosity because curious engineers tend to dig deeper into problems rather than settling for the first solution. Curiosity can be as simple as reading the documentation of a tool more thoroughly than necessary. A team culture that rewards curiosity tends to produce more thoughtful engineering decisions.

examples.english: She took the initiative to fix the broken build without being asked.
examples.persian: او بدون این‌که از او خواسته شود، ابتکار عمل به خرج داد و بیلد خراب را تعمیر کرد.

examples.english: Managers notice initiative more than they notice someone simply following instructions.
examples.persian: مدیران ابتکار عمل را بیشتر از پیروی صرف از دستورالعمل‌ها متوجه می‌شوند.

examples.english: Taking initiative during a crisis can matter more than technical skill alone.
examples.persian: به خرج دادن ابتکار عمل در یک بحران می‌تواند مهم‌تر از صرفاً مهارت فنی باشد.

miniContext: Taking **initiative** means acting on a problem before being explicitly told to, such as fixing a recurring bug without waiting for a ticket. Initiative is often noticed more during a crisis, when someone steps up without clear instructions. Not every act of initiative turns out well, but managers usually value the willingness to try. Teams that discourage initiative often end up with employees who wait passively for instructions.

examples.english: An ownership mindset means treating the product's success as your own responsibility.
examples.persian: ذهنیت مالکیت به این معناست که موفقیت محصول را مسئولیت خودتان بدانید.

examples.english: The company tries to hire engineers with a strong ownership mindset.
examples.persian: این شرکت سعی می‌کند مهندسانی با ذهنیت مالکیت قوی استخدام کند.

examples.english: Without an ownership mindset, employees tend to do only what is explicitly assigned.
examples.persian: بدون ذهنیت مالکیت، کارمندان تمایل دارند فقط کاری را انجام دهند که صریحاً به آن‌ها محول شده است.

miniContext: An **ownership mindset** means treating a product's success or failure as personally relevant, not just someone else's responsibility. Engineers with this mindset are more likely to flag a risky decision early, even if it isn't technically their part of the system. Companies try to build an ownership mindset by giving people real decision-making power over their work. Without it, employees tend to do exactly what's asked and nothing more.

examples.english: The team's velocity dropped sharply after two engineers left the project.
examples.persian: سرعت پیشرفت تیم پس از خروج دو مهندس از پروژه به‌شدت کاهش یافت.

examples.english: Scrum masters track velocity to estimate how much work a team can complete each sprint.
examples.persian: اسکرام مسترها سرعت پیشرفت تیم را پیگیری می‌کنند تا تخمین بزنند تیم در هر اسپرینت چه مقدار کار می‌تواند انجام دهد.

examples.english: Adding new people to a struggling team rarely increases velocity right away.
examples.persian: افزودن افراد جدید به تیمی که مشکل دارد به‌ندرت سرعت پیشرفت را فوراً افزایش می‌دهد.

miniContext: **Velocity** is a metric many agile teams use to estimate how much work they can realistically complete in a sprint. A sudden drop in velocity can signal a problem, such as unclear requirements or an underlying technical issue slowing the team down. Velocity should be used to plan, not to compare different teams, since team sizes and types of work vary. Chasing a higher velocity number without attention to quality often backfires later.

meaning: چابک و کم‌هزینه از نظر فرایند

examples.english: The startup followed a lean approach, testing ideas before building full features.
examples.persian: استارتاپ رویکردی چابک و کم‌هزینه را دنبال کرد و ایده‌ها را پیش از ساخت ویژگی‌های کامل آزمایش می‌کرد.

examples.english: A lean team can sometimes move faster than a large, heavily structured one.
examples.persian: یک تیم چابک و کم‌هزینه گاهی می‌تواند سریع‌تر از یک تیم بزرگ و بسیار ساختارمند حرکت کند.

examples.english: She prefers a lean process with fewer meetings and less documentation overhead.
examples.persian: او فرایندی چابک و کم‌هزینه را با جلسات کمتر و بار اداری کمتر مستندسازی ترجیح می‌دهد.

miniContext: A **lean** approach favors testing an idea quickly and cheaply before investing heavily in building it out fully. Lean teams often ship a minimal version of a feature first, then improve it based on real user feedback. Being lean doesn't mean working carelessly; it means avoiding unnecessary steps that don't add value. Startups frequently adopt lean processes because they can't afford to waste time on the wrong priorities.

examples.english: Micromanagement made the senior developers feel like they weren't trusted.
examples.persian: مدیریت ذره‌بینی باعث شد توسعه‌دهندگان ارشد احساس کنند به آن‌ها اعتماد نمی‌شود.

examples.english: She left her last job because of constant micromanagement from her supervisor.
examples.persian: او شغل قبلی‌اش را به دلیل مدیریت ذره‌بینی مداوم سرپرستش ترک کرد.

examples.english: The new manager promised to avoid micromanagement and let the team own their decisions.
examples.persian: مدیر جدید قول داد از مدیریت ذره‌بینی پرهیز کند و اجازه دهد تیم مالک تصمیمات خودش باشد.

miniContext: **Micromanagement** happens when a manager checks in on every small detail of someone's work instead of trusting them to handle it. While it sometimes comes from good intentions, micromanagement usually signals a lack of trust and can frustrate experienced employees. Teams under micromanagement often become less willing to take initiative, since every decision gets second-guessed anyway. Avoiding micromanagement requires giving people clear goals and then stepping back.

examples.english: The company operates with a distributed team spread across five countries.
examples.persian: این شرکت با یک تیم توزیع‌شده که در پنج کشور پراکنده است فعالیت می‌کند.

examples.english: A distributed workforce requires more deliberate communication than an office-based one.
examples.persian: نیروی کار توزیع‌شده نسبت به نیروی کاری مبتنی بر دفتر، به ارتباطات دقیق‌تری نیاز دارد.

examples.english: Managing a distributed team across different time zones can be exhausting.
examples.persian: مدیریت یک تیم توزیع‌شده در مناطق زمانی مختلف می‌تواند خستگی‌آور باشد.

miniContext: A **distributed** team works from multiple locations, sometimes across several countries and time zones, rather than from a single office. Managing a distributed team well usually requires more written documentation, since quick in-person conversations aren't an option. Distributed teams can access a wider pool of talent, but coordinating schedules and meetings becomes more complex. Companies that handle distributed work successfully tend to invest heavily in clear communication tools.

meaning: با اولویت کار از راه دور

examples.english: The company redesigned its processes to become truly remote-first.
examples.persian: شرکت فرایندهای خود را بازطراحی کرد تا واقعاً با اولویت کار از راه دور عمل کند.

examples.english: A remote-first culture means meetings are planned around async communication, not the other way around.
examples.persian: فرهنگ با اولویت کار از راه دور یعنی جلسات حول ارتباط ناهمزمان برنامه‌ریزی می‌شوند، نه برعکس.

examples.english: Being remote-first forced managers to document decisions instead of relying on hallway conversations.
examples.persian: اولویت‌دادن به کار از راه دور، مدیران را مجبور کرد تصمیمات را مستند کنند به‌جای تکیه بر گفتگوهای راهرویی.

miniContext: A **remote-first** company designs its processes around remote work by default, rather than treating remote employees as an exception to an office-based culture. In a remote-first environment, decisions and discussions are usually documented in writing so that no one is excluded by time zone differences. This approach often changes how meetings are run, favoring asynchronous updates over real-time calls whenever possible. Being remote-first requires more intentional effort than simply allowing people to work from home.

examples.english: The manager tried to run inclusive meetings where everyone had a chance to speak.
examples.persian: مدیر سعی کرد جلسات فراگیری برگزار کند که در آن همه فرصت صحبت‌کردن داشته باشند.

examples.english: An inclusive hiring process helped the company build a more diverse team.
examples.persian: یک فرایند استخدام فراگیر به شرکت کمک کرد تیمی متنوع‌تر بسازد.

examples.english: She made a point of using inclusive language in her presentations.
examples.persian: او عمداً در ارائه‌هایش از زبانی فراگیر استفاده می‌کرد.

miniContext: An **inclusive** workplace makes sure that people with different backgrounds and perspectives feel able to contribute fully. Inclusive meetings, for example, might involve deliberately asking quieter participants for their opinion rather than letting the loudest voices dominate. Companies pursue inclusive hiring practices to avoid overlooking strong candidates due to unconscious bias. Being inclusive is an ongoing practice, not a single policy that gets implemented once.

examples.english: The design and engineering teams worked collaboratively to fix the usability issue.
examples.persian: تیم‌های طراحی و مهندسی به‌صورت مشارکتی برای رفع مشکل کاربردپذیری همکاری کردند.

examples.english: She prefers to solve problems collaboratively rather than deciding alone.
examples.persian: او ترجیح می‌دهد مسائل را به‌صورت مشارکتی حل کند تا به‌تنهایی تصمیم بگیرد.

examples.english: The document was written collaboratively by three different departments.
examples.persian: این سند به‌صورت مشارکتی توسط سه بخش مختلف نوشته شد.

miniContext: Working **collaboratively** means solving a problem together rather than each person working in isolation and comparing results afterward. Teams that act collaboratively tend to catch mistakes earlier, since more than one perspective is involved from the start. Writing documentation collaboratively, for instance, often produces a clearer result than one person writing alone. Still, working collaboratively takes more coordination time than working independently.

examples.english: He communicated the delay effectively, so no client was surprised later.
examples.persian: او تأخیر را به‌صورت مؤثر اطلاع داد، به‌طوری‌که بعداً هیچ مشتری غافلگیر نشد.

examples.english: The new dashboard lets managers track progress more effectively than spreadsheets did.
examples.persian: داشبورد جدید به مدیران امکان می‌دهد پیشرفت را به‌صورت مؤثرتری نسبت به صفحات گسترده پیگیری کنند.

examples.english: She was promoted for leading the migration project effectively under a tight deadline.
examples.persian: او به دلیل رهبری مؤثر پروژه مهاجرت در یک مهلت فشرده ارتقا یافت.

miniContext: Communicating **effectively** means getting your message across clearly and in a way the listener can actually use, not just technically saying the right words. A manager who delegates effectively gives enough context for someone to succeed without constant check-ins. Tools and processes can help teams work more effectively, but only if people actually use them as intended. Measuring whether something was done effectively usually requires looking at outcomes, not just effort.

examples.english: The monitoring system checks server health continuously, not just once an hour.
examples.persian: سیستم پایش سلامت سرور را به‌صورت پیوسته بررسی می‌کند، نه فقط یک‌بار در ساعت.

examples.english: She continuously improved her code review process based on team feedback.
examples.persian: او فرایند بازبینی کد خودش را بر اساس بازخورد تیم به‌صورت پیوسته بهبود داد.

examples.english: The pipeline deploys new code continuously throughout the day.
examples.persian: خط تولید نرم‌افزار کد جدید را به‌صورت پیوسته در طول روز مستقر می‌کند.

miniContext: Monitoring a system **continuously**, rather than checking it occasionally, allows teams to catch problems before users notice them. Many companies now deploy new code continuously throughout the day instead of waiting for a single large release. Improving a process continuously means making small adjustments regularly rather than waiting for an annual review. Working continuously at a high pace without breaks, however, can lead to burnout rather than better results.
